title: Elastic coverage hub for mid-cycle attrition and surge
creator: Marianne Soto
description:
Problem: Mid-cycle attrition, unplanned feature requests, and customer escalations frequently force scope cuts or emergency reassignments. Current approaches (ad-hoc reassignments, email/slack requests, or pulling from a small surge pool) are slow, opaque, and create downstream churn.

Proposal: Build an "Elastic Coverage Hub" — a lightweight internal marketplace + console workflow that lets teams publish short-term capacity needs (2-10 days) and lets other teams offer coverage or loan engineers for discrete slices of work. The hub enforces guardrails (skill match, handoff checklist, paired onboarding windows), tracks time accounting, and automates approval routing to managers.

Core components:
- Coverage request form (Console): required fields (impact, minimal acceptance criteria, onboarding docs, expected effort and overlap window) and automatic suggested responders using skills/ownership signals.
- Match engine: rules to find eligible teams/people (skill tags, on-call load, project priority, personal time-off) and rank suggestions by friction score.
- Approval flow: auto-approval for within-team swaps under 3 days; manager approval otherwise; explicit opt-in for engineers.
- Accounting & telemetry: time-tracking tags, cost-centers, and dashboards to show coverage usage, mean time-to-fill, and downstream rework rate.
- Guardrails: maximum cumulative loan time per engineer per quarter, enforced paired handoff, and mandatory handback retro.

Goals & success metrics:
- Reduce emergency scope cuts by 40% for mid-cycle incidents in Q2 2026.
- Median time-to-fill coverage request < 48 hours for requests <= 3 engineers.
- Engineer satisfaction (post-coverage survey) >= 4/5 for covered handoffs.
- Trackable reduction in thrown-over-the-wall rework (measured via postmortem linkage) by 30%.

Out-of-scope for MVP: long-term reassignments (>6 weeks), hiring, payroll implications beyond time tags, and changes to compensation.

Risk & mitigation: risk of overloading small teams -> limit weekly out-bound coverage per team and provide opt-out windows; risk of poor matching -> initial rollout to cross-functional platform teams and volunteer pool, iterate on matching weights with usage data.

MVP deliverables: Console request UI, match engine basic rule set, approval API endpoints, time-tagging integration with billing dashboard, and a lightweight PM/Eng playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Console: coverage request form live in sandbox and validated with 3 pilot teams
Matching: top-3 suggested matches surface consistently within 30s for 90% of requests
Approval: manager/owner approval flows work end-to-end with email/Slack notifications
Accounting: coverage time tags appear in team usage dashboard and link to cost centers
Playbook: handoff checklist + post-handoff retro template published in Confluence

decisions: MVP will limit individual coverage loans to 10 days and total quarterly loaned days per engineer to 30 days
Matching will start rule-based (skills + bandwidth) and iterate to a ML score only after 3 months of usage data
Time accounting will be implemented via tagging in existing usage pipelines rather than a separate payroll integration
tradeoffs: Speed vs accuracy: initial rule-based matching is faster to ship but will surface less ideal matches compared to a learned model
Governance vs agility: manager approvals slow down small requests; auto-approval under 3 days reduces friction at some risk of misuse
Scope: bundling accounting in MVP keeps Finance visibility but defers deeper payroll/workflow automations
notes: This ticket is intended as the cross-functional PM owner for the Elastic Coverage Hub MVP. After pilot, we'll iterate and consider Dedicated pool integration for larger enterprise escalations.
